paper text.text: Put $H_0=B+ac+cd+bd$. For the simple faces following $P_1,P_2$, the graph $H_{\mathrm{simp}}$ contains $H_0$. The edge $af$ excludes $(P_1;s_2,t_2)$. For $(P_2;s_1,t_1)$, we have $H_{\mathrm{rep}}=H_0$, while $H_{\mathrm{simp}}$ consists of the cycle $abfea$ and the edge $af$, which can be drawn inside that cycle without crossings. Thus Lemma~\ref{dis:joint-test} makes $G$ toroidal exactly when $H_0$ is planar, also with any allowed minor in place of $B$. Keeping $B$, the edge $cd$ and the paths $apc,brd$, then contracting these paths to $ac,bd$, shows that $H_0$ is a minor of $G$ and has no $K_5$ minor. It is nonplanar, so it contains a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with attachment set $A$ and the path $acdb$ as the fixed planar graph. This gives an allowed minor $B'$ with at most nine interior vertices and $B'+ac+cd+bd$ nonplanar. Thus $(\Psi_1\cup B')+af$ is nontoroidal, so minimality gives $B'=B$. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists these forms with no required subdivision edges. Adjoining $\Psi_1$ and $af$ to each candidate gives a graph with a $K_5$ minor or a proper nontoroidal minor~\supp{E3}, a contradiction. Hence $B$ has the required disk drawing, and Lemma~\ref{dis:four-root-isolation} makes $D$ a single vertex.

vertex names: a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t2, e = s3, f = t3; twins p, q on {a, c, e} and r, z on {b, d, f}; the paths are the edges ab, cd, ef. Interior vertices of B are i0, i1, ...
the case: G = (Psi_1 ∪ B) + af, where B has attachments A = {a, b, c, d}. The candidates are the graphs B of Construction 3.17 with attachments A, added edges E = {ac, cd, bd} and no required edges: A independent in B, interior nonempty and connected, every attachment with an interior neighbour, and B + E nonplanar (each candidate gives a Kuratowski subgraph).
verdicts: Every candidate gets a proper nontoroidal minor obtained by deleting or contracting one edge of G (a contraction merges the second vertex into the first). The witness says why that minor is nontoroidal.
